text:
maria: Quick spike idea: support manifest-less progressive streaming for safetensors by shipping a tiny sidecar index (\.sidx) alongside the checkpoint. goal: let loaders start streaming useful layers before full manifest ingestion, reduce tail latency on cold starts.

tom: explain the sidecar shape and who produces it?

maria: sidx is produced at ingest-time by the uploader service (or lazily by a sidecar that watches object writes). it contains per-chunk byte ranges, layer boundary offsets (if available), and chunk checksums. tiny and content-addressable. example: ```
.sidx: [
  {"chunk_id":"c0","start":0,"end":1048576,"boundary":"layer:0","sha256":"..."},
  {"chunk_id":"c1","start":1048576,"end":2097152,"boundary":"layer:3","sha256":"..."}
]
```

jin: Do we duplicate metadata that manifest already has? risk of staleness?

maria: good point. strategy: canonical manifest still authoritative. sidx is a derived, optional assist. upload path writes sidx atomically with checkpoint (write sidx.tmp -> mv). if sidx missing or stale, loader falls back to manifest path. we add a quick validation at runtime: compare sidx root checksum with manifest-recorded index-hash. if mismatch, ignore sidx.

sam: what's the loader contract? legacy loaders expect manifest -> chunk iterator. how do we bridge?

maria: loader-negotiation protocol: loader queries transport for an index. transport returns either: manifest, sidx, or both. if sidx present and verified, runtime can start streaming aligned-to-layer reads. we provide a small compatibility proxy (stream-proxy) that exposes a chunk-iterator view derived from sidx for old loaders. new loaders can consume sidx directly.

jin: how about safetensors partial-layer reads? Are offsets safe across quantized variants?

maria: offsets we record are raw byte offsets from the stored file. for quantized variants we store per-variant sidx or annotate sidx entries with variant tags. uploader emits sidx.variant=quant-q4_0 etc. when variant mismatch occurs we fall back. this keeps sidx tiny because only variants that need streaming get separate sidxs.

tom: IO amplification risk: if sidx causes many small range reads, we may hurt egress and IOPS.

maria: mitigation: sidx entries include a coalescing-hint: contiguous_preload_block=N bytes. runtime uses that to issue fewer larger ranged reads. also sidx includes a preferred_transport hint (mmap-friendly vs http-range) so scheduler picks best path.

sam: ops playbook for bad sidx?

maria: plan: 1) if sidx causes verify failures > X/min, disable sidx usage for that namespace. 2) fallback to manifest-only path. 3) re-ingest pipeline to rebuild sidx if uploader bug suspected. add a CircuitBreaker metric for sidx_verify_fail.

jin: rollout plan? we don't want to flip everything at once.

maria: stepwise: a) enable sidx for a handful of internal models and namespaces. b) run compatibility harness that fuzzes byte-range off-by-one, partial writes, gzipped artifacts. c) enable stream-proxy for legacy loaders in canary. d) opt-in for Dedicated clusters, default off for private.

qa-bot: queued fuzz job: sidx-offby1-check for model "code-l0" on canary namespace. ETA 2h. :robot_face:

tom: telemetry: expose sidx_used, sidx_fallback, sidx_verify_time, sidx_coalesce_efficiency. we need to see if sidx actually reduces cold-start latency.

maria: yep. also emit a sample hotstart-trace event with timeline: index_fetch, verify, first-layer-ready, runtime-ready.

sam: one more: how to handle re-sharding / object composition? if a checkpoint is uploaded as a tar of shards, sidx must reference object ids + ranges.

maria: sidx entry can include object_id + range. manifest ingestion stage that composes multi-object checkpoints will synthesize a composed_sidx referencing parts. streaming runtime will request ranges from multiple objects as needed.

jin: sounds reasonable. docs + quick demo would help convince infra and eng-runtime.

maria: I'll write a 1-pager and a demo loader that uses stream-proxy. will include the fuzz harness and the ops checklist. thanks for the feedback.

sam: nice. :thumbsup:
